subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw core own an integrated opt-in safe-update transaction that snapshots state, runs real post-update checks, and restores or rolls back package, config, plugin, workspace, and session state on failure?
rationale: The remaining work defines core updater scope, restore semantics, retention, secret handling, live smoke criteria, and coordination with narrower update, backup, scanner, and updater-architecture items; automation cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Sponsor scoped core safe update
options.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Use the open auto-update, backup/restore, upgrade-scanner, and external-updater issues as implementation tracks while keeping this issue as the umbrella reference.

options.title: Keep rollback outside core for now
options.body: Document manual recovery and external kits for now, declining automatic state restore until the updater architecture changes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped core safe update
recommendation.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior live keep-open product review and has the strongest observed connection to updater design and recent update safety history.
